take_homes: Access and use are different numbers. We report licences, but nobody tracks whether people changed how they work.
Ask what would have to be true for a colleague to drop what they do today. Don't ask how to get them to adopt the tool.
Start with one colleague and one question about how they do their job now. Don't launch a programme.

monday.move: Ask one person on my team how they prepare the quarterly pipeline review today, and don't mention AI.
monday.who: One of my business development managers, someone sceptical
monday.stop_condition: If the answer is 'it works fine, I don't want to change it', I drop it and don't build anything.
monday.blocker: The calendar is full of steering groups and I might skip it. It also doesn't show me anything an agent would do better, since the exercises were hidden behind prompts.

misconception.why: It was candid about a project that stalled, which the earlier programmes never were. But I never saw an agent do anything I couldn't have done two years ago. Every demo was '[You paste prompt...]'. So 'wait and see' still looks safe. What shook it is that the absorption problem is real, and it applies to AI the same as to the last three programmes.

one_line: The part about people not using tools they've been given is right, and the author admits his own project stalled. But the context notes are the same slides as the last programme, and I never saw the agent do anything.
